entities.summary: Władysław Wiktoryn Siciński was a member of the Polish–Lithuanian nobility and dignitary of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. Lord Master-of-the-Table and Lord Vice-Justice of Upytė, he was among the deputies of the Trakai Voivodeship nobility to the Sejm of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth of 1652 which took place during the Khmelnytsky Uprising. He is credited with using the liberum veto for the first time in Polish-Lithuanian history during the Sejm. Some historians have speculated that he might have acted on orders from Janusz Radziwiłł, though Wisner observed there is no evidence to support this theory.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Siciński's use of liberum veto in 1652 marked a significant shift in Polish-Lithuanian politics, as it gave individual deputies the power to block legislation and limit the authority of the Sejm. This move had regional implications for the governance of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth during the Khmelnytsky Uprising.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Siciński's use of liberum veto in 1652 led to a shift in Polish-Lithuanian politics, as it limited the power of the Sejm and allowed for more individualistic decision-making. This innovation had significant regional implications for the Commonwealth.
